questions.text: How is cross-correlation filtering G = F ⊗ I defined, given an image I and a filter F? Write the formula and explain the variables.

We want to apply this 2D convolutional filter ([-1,0,1; -2,0,2; -1,0,1]) as two separate 1D convolutional filters sequentially for more efficiency. Write two separate 1D convolutional filters that, applied sequentially, would produce the same result as the single 2D convolutional filter.

How many operations (addition, multiplication) would it take to apply sequentially two 1D 1×3 filters compared to one equivalent 2D filter 3×3? Give the number of operations per pixel for each case, in the general case ignoring boundary artifacts and assuming same padding at the image boundaries.
How do you need to modify a 2D cross-correlation filter to represent a 2D convolution filter?
Write down the steps of the Canny Edge Detector algorithm.
Explain hysteresis thresholding. Why is it better than a simple thresholding?
If we have a photo with salt and pepper noise, what problem(s) might we face when applying the Canny Edge Detection algorithm? What might be a possible approach to mitigate the problem?
The Harris corner response function R can be expressed by the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2 of the second-moment matrix. Explain the influence of the image content on these eigenvalues.
Briefly describe what automatic scale selection is in the context of feature descriptors and how it works.
To which of these transformations is the Harris Detector invariant? Justify your answer! — Affine transformations?
To which of these transformations is the Harris Detector invariant? Justify your answer! — Euclidean transformations?
Once keypoints have been extracted, we want to extract features for matching using SIFT. What is the dimension of a SIFT feature descriptor? Explain how you get to this number in words.
To estimate a homography H we solve an equation of the form Ah=0. Derive the equations for the matrix entries A given a single correspondence pair (pl, pr), where pr = Hpl.
How many correspondence pairs are needed to estimate a homography? Justify your answer.
We want to segment an image using the Markov Random Fields formulation and the graph-cut algorithm. Write the energy function E(x,y), explaining all the variables used. What is the role of each term?

questions.text: Given the energy function E(x,y), and the goal of finding the segmentation label x-hat, what would be the optimization objective?

topics: Image Segmentation with MRF and Graph Cuts

questions.text: Describe the steps of the RANSAC algorithm for the simple case of line fitting.
What changes do we need to make to RANSAC to apply it to the task of ground plane fitting in 3D point clouds?
Given the constraints of finding the ground plane in a 3D point cloud without labels using only positional information, explain why K-Means would be a poor choice.
Given the constraints of finding the ground plane in a 3D point cloud without labels using only positional information, explain why MaxFlow would be a poor choice.

questions.text: Given the constraints of finding the ground plane in a 3D point cloud without labels using only positional information, explain why Mixture of Gaussians would be a poor choice.
Briefly outline the overall approach of sliding-window object detection.
Explain the concept of a linear SVM classifier, i.e. what do we aim to find, what do we aim to maximize? Use words, not formulas.
What is the kernel trick, how does it work and why is it useful?
Given a dataset of 1000 RGB images of pedestrians, is it possible to train a linear SVM with HOG features on the given dataset to detect pedestrians in a sliding-window fashion? Justify your answer.
Boosting is used to build a strong classifier out of several weak classifiers. After training a new weak classifier hm(x), what values do we need to adjust and in which direction?
Explain how the weak classifiers used in the Viola-Jones detector work, i.e. how are the features computed and classified?

The Roerei-detector extends the Viola-Jones detector by using an irregular pattern of rectangles to compute the features for detection. Assume we want to use different shapes instead of rectangles, e.g. circles or triangles. Explain the most significant disadvantage of this idea. What could be a potential advantage?
What is the main difference and advantage of a CNN over the traditional fully-connected Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)?

A block consists of Convolution, ReLU, BatchNorm. Suppose you want to extract feature maps from RGBD images of size 100×100 using a single block with kernel size 3×3, bias, stride 1, zero padding of size 1. How many learned parameters do we need for a single block if the output depth is 10?
What is the number of parameters if we use an image of size 1000×1000 (same block definition)?
If we were to stack three more identical blocks, what is the receptive field that activates a pixel in the 4th layer of the CNN? Ignore the effect of BatchNorm on the receptive field.

You want to keep the same number of convolutions, but improve the receptive field of the model by adding some additional layers to the model. What methods can you suggest to improve the receptive field?

What would the 4×4 input ([3,1,1,8; 6,2,2,4; 2,5,2,3; 1,3,1,7]) look like after sequentially applying 2×2 Max Pooling, and Max Unpooling operations with stride s=2? What is the difference between Unpooling and Max Unpooling?
For the first set of images showing a convolution operation, write the name of the convolution operation, the kernel size k, the input size i, the stride s, and the padding size p.

Write a function that computes the camera center based on the camera projection matrix. Use python syntax or pseudo-code and assume numpy is imported. Loops are not allowed.
Given a stereo setup with two cameras, name all the requested elements (image plane, focal length, projected point, etc.) in the provided image.
Derive the epipolar constraint, given the calibration (rotation R and translation T) and the points X′ and X. Explicitly give the equation for the essential matrix E.

Assume you want to estimate a homography with RANSAC and you know that the proportion of outliers is given by δ. Derive the equation for the minimum number of iterations k needed such that the probability P(fail) of all iterations to fail is less than ε.

In projective Structure-from-Motion (SfM), given m images of n fixed 3D points Xj visible in each image, projective SfM can only be solved when 2mn ≥ 11m + 3n − 15. Explain the reasoning behind the different terms.
